reader.requirement: When a program's PROGRAM-ID lies between another program's PROGRAM-ID and that other program's end header (it is contained), its end program header must come before the container's; headers written in reversed order, at any nesting depth, are refused.
reader.edition-search: EndMarkerPass.cs grepped for Edition.|Year|CobolVersion: only the EditionContext parameter used to position and emit COBOL2793; no edition comparison. The grammar rules programUnit/nestedProgram/endProgramHeader carry no edition predicate; the pass is called unconditionally from BinderDriver (line 90).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb988-end-program-order-reversed covers two levels; reversal at the inner pair and outer pair of three-level nesting is not witnessed

probes.printed: COBOL2793 END PROGRAM EP9B stands where the end marker of 'EP9C' belongs (SR3); COBOL2793 END PROGRAM EP9C stands where the end marker of 'EP9B' belongs (SR3)
probes.expected: refused: A contains B contains C; END PROGRAM B before END PROGRAM C

probes.printed: COBOL2793 END PROGRAM EP11A stands where the end marker of 'EP11B' belongs (SR3); COBOL2793 END PROGRAM EP11B stands where the end marker of 'EP11A' belongs (SR3)

accepted: C, B, A in order

reader.notes: ScreenProgram pairs each header with the innermost open unit and reports SR3 when the name is a still-open container or a program the unit contains, so every reversal is refused at any depth. No edition consulted; the rule reads the same in 1985 and 2023.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:X.2.5.3 SR3. Probes at 85: re9 - contained COMMON program RE9B, END PROGRAM RE9A before END PROGRAM RE9B: refused COBOL2793 x2 'END PROGRAM RE9A stands where the end marker of PROGRAM-ID RE9B belongs'. re1 - three-level nesting with the innermost header missing so END PROGRAM B and END PROGRAM A each arrive early: refused COBOL2793 at both. re5 - siblings each ended before the container's header: accepted ('B / C'). No later-edition form of this rule exists to refuse (the ordering rule reads the same); class c not applicable beyond re6 (END FUNCTION, refused). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:X.2.5.3 SR3  (2.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3'.
